mainTopic: Does the ציץ make a קרבן פסח acceptable when it turns out the owner was impure because of זיבה? A proof from a ברייתא of רבי יוסי, its rejection, and a challenge to that rejection.
overview: This amud begins in the middle of a ברייתא of רבי יוסי. A שומרת יום כנגד יום had a פסח offered for her on her watching day and then saw blood. She may not eat it, but she is exempt from פסח שני. The גמרא suggests the reason is that the ציץ made her קרבן acceptable. It rejects this: רבי יוסי holds that her new impurity starts only from now on (מכאן ולהבא), so she was pure when the פסח was offered. The גמרא then challenges this with another ברייתא where רבי יוסי says such people make משכב ומושב impure retroactively. It answers that the retroactive impurity is only מדרבנן, and it proves this from the exchange between רבי אושעיא and רבי יוחנן. Next, the גמרא asks what רבי חייא's rule ('טומאת התהום only for a מת') excludes according to רבי יוסי. It tries to prove from this that טומאת התהום is permitted for a כהן, but that proof is rejected. It also shows how a full זבה is possible under רבי יוסי. Finally, רב יוסף asks whether טומאת התהום is permitted for a כהן offering the תמיד, and רבה begins a קל וחומר that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the ברייתא: she does not eat but is exempt from פסח שני
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא of רבי יוסי concludes: a שומרת יום כנגד יום whose פסח was offered on her second day, and who then saw blood, does not eat from it, but is exempt from פסח שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: [A woman who keeps watch a day for a day, for whom they slaughtered and sprinkled the פסח] on her second day, and afterward she saw blood: she does not eat, and she is exempt from bringing פסח שני.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא it quoted as possible proof about the ציץ. The ruling is that the woman cannot eat the פסח, but she does not need to bring פסח שני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שומרת יום כנגד יום immerses on her clean watching day, but if she sees blood later that same day, her immersion is undone. Here the פסח was offered after her immersion, and then she saw blood. She is now impure, so she cannot eat. Still, her original קרבן counts, so she does not owe פסח שני.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who saw blood during the days between her נדה periods and must wait one clean day for each day she saw
On her second day, meaning her watching day after she saw blood
She does not eat from the קרבן
The make-up פסח brought a month later by those who missed the first one

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume that 'exempt from פסח שני' means she may eat. She may NOT eat, because she is impure now. The exemption only means her first קרבן was valid, so she has already fulfilled her obligation.

phrases.english: on her second day,
phrases.notes: This continues the ברייתא from the previous עמוד, about a שומרת יום כנגד יום for whom they slaughtered and sprinkled.

phrases.english: and afterward she saw [blood] —
she does not eat,
and she is exempt from performing the second Pesach.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַחַר כָּךְ רָאֲתָה אֵינָהּ אוֹכֶלֶת וּפְטוּרָה מִלַּעֲשׂוֹת פֶּסַח שֵׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא cited (on the previous עמוד) as a proof about whether the ציץ helps for טומאת זיבה.
steps.raayaObject: Whether the ציץ makes a קרבן acceptable when the owner turns out to have doubtful טומאה from זיבה
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא in the name of רבי יוסי about a שומרת יום כנגד יום

steps.title: The inference: the exemption must be because the ציץ helps
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why she is exempt from פסח שני and suggests it must be because the ציץ made her קרבן acceptable.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason she is exempt? Is it not because the ציץ makes it acceptable?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pulls the proof out of the ברייתא. It asks for the reason behind the exemption and proposes that it is the ציץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she was really impure when the פסח was offered, her קרבן should not count, and she should owe פסח שני. Her exemption suggests something fixed the problem, namely the ציץ. That would show the ציץ helps even for טומאה connected to זיבה.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
Is it not because…? (introduces a suggested reason)
The golden frontplate of the כהן גדול
Makes acceptable; brings atonement so the קרבן is valid

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Is it not because the frontplate appeases [makes it acceptable]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the intended proof out of the ברייתא quoted in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That the ציץ helps for טומאה connected to a זבה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The exemption from פסח שני in רבי יוסי's ברייתא

steps.title: Rejection: רבי יוסי holds her impurity starts only from now
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The exemption may come from רבי יוסי's view that her new sighting makes her impure only from now on, so she was truly pure when the פסח was offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: No. It is because רבי יוסי holds that she makes things impure only from now onward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. It offers a different reason for the exemption, one that has nothing to do with the ציץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If her impurity begins only at the moment she sees blood (מכאן ולהבא), then at the time of the שחיטה and זריקה she was completely pure. Her קרבן was valid on its own, without any help from the ציץ. So the ברייתא proves nothing about the ציץ.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds (this view)
From now and onward, not retroactively
She makes things impure

phrases.english: They say: No,
[rather, it is] because Rabbi Yosei holds:
she renders impure from now and onward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference of step 2 by offering an alternative explanation of the ruling.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the ברייתא that the ציץ helps for זיבה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The exemption can be explained without the ציץ, since according to רבי יוסי she was actually pure at the time of the offering (מכאן ולהבא).

steps.title: Challenge: רבי יוסי elsewhere says the impurity is retroactive
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rejection with another ברייתא of רבי יוסי. A זב on his seventh day and a שומרת יום כנגד יום on her second day who see again make משכב ומושב impure retroactively, and yet they are exempt from פסח שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יוסי says, a זב who had two sightings, for whom they slaughtered and sprinkled on his seventh day, and afterward he saw; and similarly a שומרת יום כנגד יום for whom they slaughtered and sprinkled on her second day, and afterward she saw: these make a bed and a seat impure retroactively, and they are exempt from bringing פסח שני.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rejection from step 3. It quotes רבי יוסי saying the impurity in such a case IS retroactive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רבי יוסי says these people make משכב ומושב impure למפרע, back to the time of their immersion. So he does not hold מכאן ולהבא, and they were impure when the פסח was offered. Yet they are still exempt from פסח שני, which brings back the ציץ as the likely reason. The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: A זב who had two discharges and must count seven clean days
On his seventh clean day
Items made for lying and sitting, which a זב makes impure
Retroactively

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי rules that a זב or a שומרת יום כנגד יום who sees again makes משכב ומושב impure retroactively, yet is exempt from פסח שני. At this point that seems to undercut the מכאן ולהבא explanation, but step 5 answers that the retroactive impurity is only מדרבנן, and step 11 proves it.
steps.whyThisMatters: If the retroactive impurity were Torah law, the owner would have been truly impure at the time of the קרבן, and the exemption from פסח שני would be strong evidence that the ציץ helps for טומאת זיבה. The next step answers this by limiting the retroactive impurity to מדרבנן.

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught: Rabbi Yosei says:
a zav who has had two sightings
for whom they slaughtered and sprinkled on his seventh day,
and afterward he saw [a discharge],
and likewise a woman who keeps watch a day for a day
for whom they slaughtered and sprinkled on her second day,
and afterward she saw —

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ מְטַמְּאִין מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב לְמַפְרֵעַ,
phrases.english: these render objects for lying and sitting impure retroactively,
and they are exempt from performing the second Pesach.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rejection in step 3 by showing that רבי יוסי holds the impurity is retroactive.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יוסי holds the impurity starts only from now (מכאן ולהבא)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי explicitly rules that משכב ומושב become impure למפרע, so the owners were impure at the time of the offering. Their exemption from פסח שני then cannot be explained by מכאן ולהבא.

steps.title: Retroactive impurity is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge: רבי יוסי's 'retroactive' impurity is only מדרבנן. מדאורייתא, the impurity starts only from the new sighting.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: What does 'retroactively' mean? It is only a rabbinic rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 4. It explains that רבי יוסי's 'retroactive' impurity is only a rabbinic rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 4 it looked like רבי יוסי holds a full retroactive impurity, which would make the קרבן פסח offered in impurity. The answer is that מדאורייתא she became impure only from the new sighting, so the פסח was offered in purity. The retroactive impurity on משכב ומושב is a rabbinic stringency. So the דחיה from step 3 still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Retroactively, going backward in time
By rabbinic law, not Torah law

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יוסי has two opposite opinions. מדאורייתא the impurity starts only from now on. The retroactive impurity is only a rabbinic extra rule.

phrases.english: They say:
What is 'retroactively'? It is by rabbinic law.
phrases.notes: Under Torah law the impurity starts only from the new sighting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 4 and saves the דחיה of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the levels of law: retroactive impurity is rabbinic, Torah impurity is from now on.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי holds a full Torah-level retroactive impurity, so the פסח was offered in impurity.
steps.terutzMaskana: מדאורייתא she was pure when the פסח was offered. The retroactive impurity is only מדרבנן, so she is still exempt from פסח שני.

steps.title: Support from the debate of רבי אושעיא and רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רבי אושעיא also understood that retroactive impurity is מדרבנן. It quotes a ברייתא: a זב who sees on his seventh day cancels all the earlier days, and רבי יוחנן replies that it cancels only that day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even רבי אושעיא holds that he makes things impure retroactively only by rabbinic law. As it was taught: רבי אושעיא says, 'But a זב who saw on his seventh day cancels the days before it.' רבי יוחנן said to him: 'It should cancel only its own day!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a proof for the answer in step 5. It quotes the debate between רבי אושעיא and רבי יוחנן, which it will analyze in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זב must count seven clean days. Normally a sighting during those days cancels the count. רבי אושעיא says a sighting even on the seventh day cancels all the earlier days. רבי יוחנן seems to say it cancels only the day of the sighting. The real proof comes later, from what רבי אושעיא says back to him.

keyTerms.meaning: A man made impure by a discharge; he must count seven clean days
Cancels the clean days before it, so the count starts again
'Its day': the day of the sighting itself

phrases.english: And even Rabbi Oshaya holds
that he makes things impure retroactively only by rabbinic law.
As it was taught: Rabbi Oshaya says:
But a zav who saw a discharge on his seventh day,
it cancels the days before it.
And Rabbi Yochanan said to him:
It should cancel only its own day!
phrases.notes: The next step will question this wording.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא סָבַר מְטַמֵּא לְמַפְרֵעַ מִדְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to support the answer of step 5.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוסי's retroactive impurity is only מדרבנן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי אושעיא and רבי יוחנן about a זב who sees on his seventh day.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's words make no sense either way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks רבי יוחנן's wording with a 'ממה נפשך'. If impurity is retroactive, all the days should be cancelled. If impurity is only from now on, not even the day itself should be cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whichever way you look at it: if he holds that the impurity is retroactive, all the days should be cancelled. If he holds that the impurity is only from now on, even his own day should not be cancelled!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רבי יוחנן's reply ('only its day') does not fit either possible view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the sighting reaches back in time, the seventh day is ruined, and a sighting during the count cancels everything before it. If the sighting counts only from now on, part of the seventh day was already clean. Part of a day counts as a full day, so the seven days were completed. Cancelling exactly one day is a middle position with no logic behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Whichever way you want': a challenge showing that both options fail
He holds, he is of the opinion
From now on, not backward in time

phrases.english: Whichever way you look at it:
If he holds that he makes things impure retroactively,
then it should cancel all of them, even all the days.

phrases.aramaic: אִי קָסָבַר מִכָּאן וּלְהַבָּא הוּא מְטַמֵּא —
phrases.english: If he holds that he makes things impure only from now on,
then it should not cancel even his own day!
phrases.notes: The part of the seventh day before the sighting counts as a clean day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of רבי יוחנן's reply quoted in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's statement 'לֹא יִסְתּוֹר אֶלָּא יוֹמוֹ'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both the 'retroactive' view and the 'from now on' view lead to a result other than cancelling exactly one day.

steps.title: Fixing the wording: not even its own day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the reading of רבי יוחנן's words to 'it does not cancel, not even its own day'. This fits the 'from now on' view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: It does not cancel, and not even its own day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the problem by changing the reading of רבי יוחנן's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now רבי יוחנן clearly holds that the impurity starts only from now on, so the seven clean days stay complete. This sets up a clear contrast: רבי יוחנן holds 'from now on', and רבי אושעיא holds 'cancels everything'.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather, say': the גמרא fixes the reading of a text

phrases.english: Rather, say:
It does not cancel, and not even its own day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֵימָא: לֹא יִסְתּוֹר וְלֹא יוֹמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ממה נפשך of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changes the reading of the text.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן said the sighting cancels only its own day.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן said it cancels nothing, not even its own day, because the impurity starts only from now on.

steps.title: רבי אושעיא: רבי יוסי agrees with you
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא tells רבי יוחנן that רבי יוסי holds like him, meaning that the impurity starts only from now on.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he said to him: רבי יוסי stands with your opinion.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אושעיא answers רבי יוחנן: 'רבי יוסי agrees with you.' This sets up the key question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אושעיא is probably thinking of רבי יוסי's ruling that this person is exempt from פסח שני. That ruling shows that the impurity starts only from now on, like רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Stands with you, holds like your opinion

phrases.english: And he said to him:
Rabbi Yosei stands with your opinion.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי קָאֵי כְּווֹתָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא: רבי אושעיא's response to the corrected words of רבי יוחנן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי holds like רבי יוחנן that the impurity starts only from now on.

steps.title: But רבי יוסי says the impurity is retroactive
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי יוסי can hold like רבי יוחנן, when רבי יוסי rules that משכב ומושב become impure retroactively.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי יוסי says they make משכב and מושב impure retroactively!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אושעיא's claim. רבי יוסי himself speaks of retroactive impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same ברייתא of רבי יוסי from step 4. It seems to show that רבי יוסי holds the opposite of רבי יוחנן's 'from now on' view. The answer to this question will be the proof the גמרא is looking for.

keyTerms.meaning: Objects made for lying or sitting, which a זב makes impure
'But surely': introduces a contradiction

phrases.english: But surely Rabbi Yosei says:
They make objects for lying and sitting impure retroactively!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אושעיא's claim in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יוסי holds like רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי rules that impurity is retroactive, and רבי יוחנן holds it is only from now on.

steps.title: Conclusion: retroactive impurity is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: The only way רבי יוסי can agree with רבי יוחנן is if his retroactive impurity is מדרבנן. The גמרא accepts this conclusion.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, is it not so? Learn from this that he makes things impure retroactively only by rabbinic law. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that רבי יוסי's retroactive impurity is only a rabbinic rule, and it accepts this as proven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מדאורייתא, רבי יוסי holds 'from now on', like רבי יוחנן. That is why he exempts the person from פסח שני. The retroactive impurity on משכב ומושב is only a rabbinic stringency. This confirms the answer of step 5, and the proof from the ציץ in step 2 stays rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather, is it not so?': leads to the only remaining explanation
'Learn from it': the point is proven

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוסי, a זב or זבה who sees again is impure מדאורייתא only from the moment of the new sighting. The retroactive impurity on משכב ומושב is only מדרבנן. So a פסח offered before the new sighting was offered in purity, and the exemption from פסח שני does not prove that the ציץ made the קרבן acceptable.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the attempt from step 2 to prove that the ציץ makes the קרבן of a טמא acceptable.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not so? Learn from this:
he makes things impure retroactively only by rabbinic law.
Indeed, learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 10 and proves the answer of step 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוסי's retroactive impurity of a זב or זבה is מדרבנן. מדאורייתא the impurity begins only from the new sighting.

steps.title: According to רבי יוסי, what does רבי חייא's rule exclude?
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי יוסי holds a זב's impurity is only from now on, the earlier answer (that רבי חייא excludes זב and זבה) no longer works. So what does 'only למת' exclude?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי יוסי, now that he said a זב makes things impure only from now on, what does 'only for a מת' come to exclude?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רבי חייא's rule that טומאת התהום was permitted only for impurity of a מת. It asks what that word 'only' leaves out, if we follow רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the 'only' was explained as excluding a זב or זבה whose new sighting makes the קרבן impure backwards in time. But רבי יוסי says that by Torah law the impurity starts only from now on, so the קרבן was never impure and there is nothing to exclude. So the word 'only' needs a new target.

keyTerms.meaning: Impurity from a hidden, unknown source (such as a buried body nobody knew about)
From now on (not backwards in time)
To exclude what?
Only

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Yosei,
now that he said
he (the zav) renders impure only from now on,
phrases.notes: By Torah law there is no retroactive impurity (see Step 11).

phrases.english: then Rabbi Chiya's 'only for a corpse' comes to exclude what?
phrases.notes: This refers back to רבי חייא's rule: טומאת התהום was permitted only for impurity of a מת.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי, הַשְׁתָּא דְּאָמַר מִכָּאן וּלְהַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the conclusion about רבי יוסי (Step 11) back to the earlier proof from רבי חייא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What case the word 'only' in רבי חייא's rule excludes, according to רבי יוסי.

steps.title: Proof that טומאת התהום is permitted for a כהן
steps.stepSummary: If the 'only' cannot exclude זב, it must exclude impurity from a שרץ. That only matters for a כהן, so it proves טומאת התהום is permitted for a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us settle the question from this: the rule is talking about a כהן, and טומאת התהום was permitted for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to use רבי חייא's rule to answer the open question of whether טומאת התהום is permitted for the כהן who does the עבודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With זב out of the picture, the only thing left to exclude is impurity from a שרץ. The assumption is that we may slaughter and sprinkle for an owner who is impure from a שרץ, because he can immerse and be pure by evening. So an owner's שרץ impurity never needs forgiving, and the rule must be talking about the כהן. That would mean טומאת התהום (from a מת) is permitted for a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us settle (the question) from it
The priest who performs the service
Was permitted

phrases.english: Let us resolve the question from this,
that it speaks of a priest, and it was permitted for him:
the impurity of the deep.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 12 in a way that settles the larger question about the כהן.
steps.raayaObject: That טומאת התהום is permitted for a כהן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי חייא's rule 'only for a מת', which must now exclude שרץ, and that only matters for a כהן.

steps.title: The rule can be about owners of a קרבן פסח
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. The rule is really about the owners bringing a קרבן פסח, and רבי חייא holds you may not offer it for people impure from a שרץ, so the exclusion is needed for them too.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: really it speaks about the owners, and about the קרבן פסח. רבי חייא holds that we do not slaughter and sprinkle the blood for people impure from a שרץ, so he needed to exclude that case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof from Step 13. It shows that the exclusion of שרץ can make sense even when we talk about the owners, not the כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed that a שרץ-impure owner never matters. But for the קרבן פסח, רבי חייא may hold that we do not offer it for someone impure from a שרץ. So he had to teach that an unknown שרץ impurity of the owners is not forgiven. Now the rule proves nothing about a כהן, and the question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually (introduces the true reading)
The owners of the offering
People impure from touching a dead creeping creature
Slaughtering and sprinkling the blood

steps.confusionAlert: This does not say רבי חייא's rule is about the כהן and is false. It only shows the rule can also be read as being about the owners, so it cannot serve as a proof.

phrases.english: They say: actually, it is about the owners and about the Paschal lamb,
and he (Rabbi Chiya) holds: we do not slaughter and sprinkle
for people impure from a creeping animal,
and so it was necessary to exclude (that case).

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. It does not decide the question about a כהן either way.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed שרץ impurity of the owners never matters. For a קרבן פסח, under רבי חייא's view, it does matter.
steps.whatToRemember: The attempt to prove from רבי חייא that טומאת התהום is permitted for a כהן fails, because his rule can be about the owners of a קרבן פסח.

steps.title: Under רבי יוסי, how can there ever be a full זבה?
steps.stepSummary: If each new sighting counts only from now on, how can three sightings ever join together to make a woman a full זבה?
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבי יוסי, how can you ever find a full זבה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new challenge against רבי יוסי's view that impurity starts only from now on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman becomes a full זבה by seeing blood three days in a row. If every new sighting starts fresh, as if it were the first one, then the sightings never join together. So it seems a full זבה could never happen, which cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: A full זבה (after three days of sightings, who needs a קרבן)
How can you find (such a case)?
But (introduces a challenge)

phrases.english: But according to Rabbi Yosei,
how can you find a full-fledged zava?
phrases.notes: If each sighting starts fresh, three sightings never link together.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי, זָבָה גְּמוּרָה הֵיכִי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבי חייא discussion and attacks רבי יוסי's 'from now on' view from a new direction.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's view that a new sighting makes impure only from now on.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If each sighting is treated as a fresh start, sightings can never add up to three, so a full זבה could never exist.

steps.title: Three sightings join when the flow is continuous or spans two twilights
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a full זבה is possible under רבי יוסי. This happens when the woman's flow is continuous, or when she sees blood through two entire בין השמשות periods.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is possible when she flows continuously. Or, if you prefer, when she saw blood during the entire twilight period on two days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 15. It shows two cases where the three days of blood are linked together, so she becomes a full זבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that each sighting seemed to start fresh, so the sightings never added up. In the first case, the blood never stops, so it is one long sighting across three days. In the second case, blood that covers a whole בין השמשות period belongs to two days at once, since twilight is in doubt between day and night. So the days connect with no clean break between them.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman whose blood flows continuously, without stopping
'If you wish, say': introduces a second, alternative answer
Twilight, the period in doubt between day and night
A woman who sees blood outside her normal time, for three days in a row

steps.confusionAlert: The two answers are separate options, not one combined case. Either answer alone is enough to solve the problem.

phrases.english: In a woman who flows continuously.
phrases.notes: The blood runs without a break across the three days.

phrases.english: If you wish, say:

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן שֶׁרָאֲתָה כׇּל שְׁנֵי בֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת.
phrases.english: For example, where she saw blood during two entire twilights.
phrases.notes: Each full twilight touches two days, so the sightings link together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the קשיא of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: the rule works in specific situations where the sightings are linked.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since each sighting counts only from now on, it seemed three sightings could never join to make a full זבה.
steps.terutzMaskana: A full זבה is possible when her flow is continuous, or when it covers two full twilights, because then the days are connected.
steps.whatToRemember: Under רבי יוסי, a זבה's impurity starts from the moment she sees blood. She can still become a full זבה when her bleeding links the days, either through a continuous flow or through bleeding during two full twilights.

steps.title: Does the deep-impurity leniency apply to a כהן offering the תמיד?
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks whether טומאת התהום is permitted for a כהן who brings the קרבן תמיד. The question is whether the oral tradition was given only for the קרבן פסח, or whether the תמיד can be learned from the פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף asked: is טומאת התהום permitted for a כהן who offers the תמיד, or not? Suppose we say that טומאת התהום is permitted for the כהן who offers the sacrifices of a נזיר and of someone bringing a פסח. What about the כהן who offers the תמיד? Do we say that the tradition about טומאת התהום was taught only for the פסח, and not for the תמיד? Or perhaps we learn the תמיד from the פסח?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב יוסף asks whether the leniency of טומאת התהום, which we know works for the קרבן פסח, also works for a כהן offering the קרבן תמיד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף does not take it as a given that the כהן offering a נזיר's or a פסח's קרבן is allowed טומאת התהום. With 'אם תמצא לומר' he assumes it only for the sake of argument, since that question was just left unresolved in step 14. His doubt is about the קרבן תמיד, the daily communal offering. Maybe the tradition (הלכה למשה מסיני) covers only the פסח, so we cannot stretch it. Or maybe we can learn the תמיד from the פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked a question that he did not know the answer to (a בעיא)
The כהן whose service makes the קרבן acceptable
The daily communal offering, brought every morning and afternoon
Impurity from a corpse hidden so deeply that no one knew about it
'We learned by tradition': a law received orally, not from a verse
He derives one law from another

steps.whyThisMatters: The question is whether a special oral tradition can be extended beyond its original case. This idea comes up often in the גמרא.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef asked:
A priest who offers the daily offering,

phrases.aramaic: הוּתְּרָה לוֹ טוּמְאַת הַתְּהוֹם אוֹ לָא?
phrases.english: is impurity of the deep permitted for him or not?
If you say
phrases.notes: Sets up an assumption to build on.

phrases.english: that the priest who offers their sacrifices
(of a nazirite and of one bringing a Pesach)
is permitted impurity of the deep,
what about a priest who offers the daily offering?

phrases.aramaic: מִי אָמְרִינַן כִּי גְּמִירִי טוּמְאַת הַתְּהוֹם —
phrases.english: Do we say that when we learned impurity of the deep by tradition,
it was for the Pesach, but for the daily offering we did not learn it?
Or perhaps we derive the daily offering from the Pesach?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question, related to the earlier discussion of טומאת התהום for a כהן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the tradition permitting טומאת התהום applies to a כהן offering the תמיד, or only to the פסח.

steps.title: רבה starts to answer with a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: רבה begins a קל וחומר. For the פסח, known impurity is not allowed, yet טומאת התהום is allowed. So for communal offerings, where even known impurity can be allowed, טומאת התהום should surely be allowed. The argument continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: there is a קל וחומר. In a place where known impurity is not permitted to him, טומאת התהום is still permitted to him. So in a place where known impurity is permitted to him, (all the more so)...
steps.whatsHappening: רבה tries to answer רב יוסף's question with a קל וחומר. His sentence is not finished here and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the קרבן פסח, someone who knows he is impure cannot bring it, yet טומאת התהום is still forgiven. Communal offerings like the תמיד are more lenient, because they may be brought even in known impurity when no pure option exists. So if the stricter case allows טומאת התהום, the more lenient case should allow it too.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument: if the strict case is lenient, the lenient case is surely lenient too
Impurity that is known about
'Just as...': the opening word of a קל וחומר

steps.confusionAlert: 'A place where known impurity is permitted' means communal offerings like the תמיד, not the פסח. The פסח is the stricter case here, where known impurity is not allowed.

phrases.english: Rabba said: it follows by a kal vachomer:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה בְּמָקוֹם שֶׁלֹּא הוּתְּרָה לוֹ טוּמְאָה יְדוּעָה —
phrases.english: Just as in a place where known impurity was not permitted to him,
impurity of the deep was permitted to him,
then a place where known impurity was permitted to him,
phrases.notes: This refers to communal offerings like the תמיד. The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer רב יוסף's question from step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Through a קל וחומר from the פסח, טומאת התהום should be permitted for the כהן offering the תמיד. The argument is completed on the next amud.
